What Is Asset Integrity Management?

Asset Integrity Management (AIM) is a structured approach that ensures industrial assets — pipelines, storage tanks, pressure vessels, offshore platforms, rotating equipment, and refinery units — are designed, operated, and maintained safely throughout their lifecycle.

Modern AIM includes:

  • Non-Destructive Testing (NDT)
  • Risk-Based Inspection (RBI)
  • Digital Twins
  • Condition Monitoring (CM)
  • Failure mode analysis
  • Maintenance planning
  • Real-time asset health dashboards

Companies adopting advanced AIM frameworks experience fewer failures, lower operational risk, and improved regulatory compliance.

Risk-Based Inspection (RBI) Framework

RBI is the foundation of modern Asset Integrity Management:

Core Principles:

  • Prioritize inspections based on risk (probability × consequence of failure)
  • Optimize inspection intervals and methods
  • Allocate resources to highest-risk assets
  • Reduce unnecessary inspections on low-risk equipment

RBI Process:

  1. Asset Inventory: Identify all pressure-containing equipment
  2. Damage Mechanism Assessment: Identify potential failure modes
  3. Probability of Failure (POF): Assess likelihood based on condition, age, operating conditions
  4. Consequence of Failure (COF): Evaluate safety, environmental, and business impact
  5. Risk Ranking: Calculate risk matrix (POF × COF)
  6. Inspection Planning: Define inspection strategy for each risk category
  7. Execution & Review: Perform inspections and update risk assessments

Benefits:

  • 30-50% reduction in inspection costs
  • Improved safety through focus on high-risk assets
  • Optimized turnaround planning
  • Better resource allocation
  • Regulatory compliance

NDT Integration in AIM

NDT is the primary tool for assessing asset condition:

Method Selection:

  • Corrosion Monitoring: UT thickness gauging, corrosion mapping
  • Crack Detection: MT, PT, PAUT, TOFD
  • Weld Inspection: RT, PAUT, TOFD
  • Structural Assessment: VT, thermography, acoustic emission

Inspection Frequency:

  • High Risk: Annual or more frequent
  • Medium Risk: 2-5 year intervals
  • Low Risk: 5-10 year intervals
  • Continuous Monitoring: Sensors for critical assets

Data Management:

Digital Twin platforms integrate NDT data for:

  • Trend analysis and degradation modeling
  • Remaining life predictions
  • Inspection planning optimization
  • Real-time risk updates

Corrosion Monitoring & Management

Corrosion Mechanisms:

  • General corrosion and wall thinning
  • Pitting and localized corrosion
  • Stress corrosion cracking (SCC)
  • Corrosion under insulation (CUI)
  • High-temperature corrosion

Monitoring Methods:

  • UT Thickness Gauging: Periodic measurements
  • Corrosion Mapping: Comprehensive thickness surveys
  • Corrosion Probes: Continuous monitoring
  • Thermography: CUI detection
  • Acoustic Emission: Active corrosion detection

Corrosion Management:

  • Corrosion loops and circuits
  • Inspection planning based on corrosion rates
  • Material selection and upgrades
  • Protective coating programs
  • Cathodic protection systems

Running this as a programme, not a one-off

If you are responsible for an inspection programme rather than a single job, the recurring problem is rarely the code — it is keeping measured thickness, damage-mechanism assignment and next-inspection dates in one defensible place. Asset integrity management software covers how RBI under API 580/581 and fitness-for-service under API 579 behave when they run on measured corrosion rates per CML instead of default rates, and what changes for the integrity team.
